Uncle Cranky Pants on Marriage

I'm almost 50 now, and have been in a gay relationship/marriage for about 30 years. I love my marriage and wouldn't trade it for anything! But I don't remember an adult saying these things to me when I was a kid, so I'm saying them here in the hopes it helps someone else.

Marriage can be wonderful, but happily ever after takes work

A marriage is work: lifelong, committed work. It can be wonderful and rewarding. But movies act like getting married is the end of the story. Getting married is just the start of a long relationship that must change over time.

It's normal to have unrealistic expectations

Most people come into a marriage with expectations about how things can or should be. These come from our parents, our family and friends, TVs/movies/books, our own hopes and dreams . . . and they are important! Without them we'd have no framework for building a relationship.

But the odds are, both people will have some expectations that just can't be met, or work for other people but not for them, or used to work for them but don't work anymore.

You can't live someone else's marriage. Over time you'll learn what works for you two, and what doesn't.

Everybody needs a space of their own and some time alone

If this doesn't happen automatically, find a way to make it happen. Make it happen for your spouse too.

Disagreements are normal and expected

You should have a few fights over the years. Life is stressful. You are two different people who change over time. That doesn't mean you should break up or that you're doing it wrong. The old setup may not work, or sometimes you just need to vent.

Abuse or constant fighting is a different thing.

Make disagreements go more smoothly

Focus on problems, not people

Assigning blame causes hurt feelings without fixing anything. If you want to have endless fights to no purpose, blaming is a great way to do it.

Be as honest with each other as you can stand to be

This is a tough one. Marriage will bring out parts of you - and your spouse - that you don't want to see.

But the more honest you can be about what you want and why, the better you'll both be able to deal with things.

Never go to bed angry

Whatever is bothering you, get it out in the open before you go to sleep! Yell at each other if you have to. No matter how bad you feel about the problem, sleeping mad makes things worse. The closest we've been to breaking up is when we went to bed angry

Never say "I told you so"

  1. You tell someone not to do something
  2. They do it
  3. Things go badly
  4. "Someone" is frustrated and sensitive. Something that was supposed to work, didn't. They made a bad call and they know it.
  5. You say, "See, I told you so."
  6. "Someone" thanks you for speaking up, praises you for your insight, and resolves to listen to you more in the future.

I don't think #6 has ever happened in the history of the world.

No adult at #4 has forgotten #1. Your reminder just rubs salt in a very fresh wound.

The correct thing to say at #5: "I'm sorry that didn't work out."

If they keep making the same mistake, you get a few more options.

#1: "Remember last time when you . . .?"

#5: "Next time, could we maybe . . . "?

But when you want to say "I told you so," stifle that as hard and as deep as you can.

Accept that you're both people with your own personalities, preferences, and limitations

Never attempt to teach a pig to sing; it wastes your time and annoys the pig.

- Robert Heilein

If your spouse expects something of you that you can't do, or vice-versa, you'll both just end up frustrated.

In MBTI terms, I'm very much a judger, my husband is very much a perceiver.

I take care of the bills, period. The last thing we need is for his random-access scheduling to miss a mortgage payment.

On the other hand, I'm happy to let him handle social obligations. He can create entertainment and a meal for six on a moment's notice. I continue to be amazed even after decades.

No marriage is perfect because no people are perfect. Accept that there are some things you're just not going to get, and enjoy what you do get.
